title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, employees and contractors
tiers.description: All Directors, employees and contractors of the Company and their associates. This tier is subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the confidentiality duty; the 'additional restrictions' in rule 6 (blackouts, short-term trading, hedging, margin/securities lending, encumbrances, clearance) are not expressed to apply to it.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors and officers including the CEO; all employees who occupy a position allowing significant influence over the management and administration of the Company, including all direct reports to the CEO ('Senior Executives'); their associates (as defined in the Takeovers Code); and other persons identified by the Company from time to time. All substantive additional restrictions attach to this tier.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair, a Restricted Person, distinguished only for clearance: must notify and obtain clearance from the Board.

tiers.name: Other Directors (including CEO)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair, including the CEO; distinguished only for clearance (Chair of the Board) and for post-trade information sufficient for NZX/ASX change of interests notices.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Employees who occupy a position allowing significant influence over management and administration, including all direct reports to the CEO; clearance from the Chair of the Board and the CEO, with post-trade change of interests information.

tiers.name: Other persons identified by the Company from time to time
tiers.description: Persons designated as Restricted Persons by the Company; clearance from the CEO.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities

windows.start_anchor: close of trading one week before the end of the full financial year
windows.end_anchor: 10.00am on the second trading day following the announcement to NZX and ASX of the preliminary final statement or full year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading one week before the end of the financial half year
windows.end_anchor: 10.00am on the second trading day following the announcement of half-yearly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may declare 'any other period that the Company specifies from time to time' as a blackout period (rule 6.3). The policy does not name the decision-maker, any notification mechanism, or whether the reason is confidential.

rules.detail: Dealing in derivatives, including put and call options and equity swaps, is expressly named and is permitted with prior written approval from the rule 7 person. There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written by a bank is squarely within the clause. 'Securities' is separately defined to include options over existing shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to the shares, so dealing in them is also a dealing subject to blackouts and rule 6.6 clearance.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: The policy draws no distinction between exchange-traded and OTC derivatives; both are caught by rule 6.9 and by the definition of Securities, and both require prior written approval and compliance with the blackout periods.
rules.evidence: “Securities” means shares, debentures, options to subscribe for new shares and options over existing shares, warrant contracts and other derivatives relating to the shares.

rules.detail: Hedging of Company Securities generally is not prohibited outright; it requires prior written approval from the rule 7 person. It remains subject to the blackout periods in 6.3 and the general insider trading prohibition, and the approval discretion is unfettered.
rules.evidence: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Unusually, hedging of unvested plan securities is not an absolute ban: the second sentence of 6.9 simply confirms that unvested plan securities fall within the same prior written approval requirement rather than carving out a prohibition.
rules.evidence: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to any employee option or share plan.

rules.detail: The rule 6 additional restrictions, including the hedging clause, are expressed to apply only to Restricted Persons. Employees and contractors who are not Restricted Persons are addressed only by the insider trading prohibition and the confidentiality duty.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and collars are not named. A monetising structure is an 'other arrangement which varies economic risk related to the Company's Securities' and a 'contract intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price', so it needs prior written approval; the funding leg is separately caught by rule 6.10.
rules.evidence: enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Expressed hortatorily ('should not') rather than as an absolute bar, and a waiver from rule 6.4 is available for exceptional circumstances under rule 6.5. A physically settled collar over shares already held is not a short sale, but a cash-settled or naked short leg would be.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending arrangements are expressly named alongside margin lending: advance notification to the rule 7 person plus written clearance before the arrangement is entered into. No prohibition.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference are named in the rule 6.9 list and so require prior written approval. In practice a CFD would also engage the rule 6.4 discouragement of short term and speculative trading and, if short, the short selling limb.
rules.evidence: including, for example, dealing in warrants, equity swaps, put and call options, contracts for difference and other contracts intended to secure a profit or avoid a loss based on fluctuations in the price of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted subject to advance notification and prior written clearance from the rule 7 person. The policy is silent on forced sales, margin calls, price triggers, gearing limits and ongoing disclosure.
rules.evidence: The proposed arrangement must not be entered into or grant made until written clearance has been given by the person nominated in rule 7.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities is expressly permitted subject to advance notification and prior written clearance. The grant is treated as its own regulated act rather than as a dealing, so rule 6.3 blackouts are not in terms applied to it, though prudence would suggest otherwise.
rules.evidence: granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities. The notification must be made to the person in rule 7.

rules.detail: There is no general ban on secured financing. Any loan secured on Company Securities is caught by the encumbrance limb of rule 6.10 and requires advance notification and written clearance; the security interest may not be granted until clearance is given. Nothing distinguishes vested from unvested shares.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities.

rules.detail: No defined holding period or LIFO rule; a general standard against short term or speculative trading, drafted as 'should not', and waivable under rule 6.5 for exceptional circumstances. A short-dated or speculative-looking collar risks characterisation under this rule.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.

clearance.post_trade_to: The Board; all Directors are to be notified of any trading in securities by Directors or Senior Executives
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately after the trade is completed
clearance.evidence: Clearance to deal in Company Securities can be revoked at any time but will otherwise be valid (unless another period is otherwise specified in the clearance) for a period of ten trading days commencing on the date following the clearance being obtained.

clearance.post_trade_to: Chair of the Board, with sufficient information to enable NZX and ASX change of interests notification; all Directors are to be notified
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately after the trade is completed
clearance.evidence: The proposed dealing must not be entered into until written clearance has been given by the person nominated in rule 7. In determining whether to clear the proposed dealing, the relevant person nominated in rule 7 will consider whether the proposed dealing is appropriate having regard to all relevant circumstances.

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board and the CEO
clearance.post_trade_to: Chair of the Board and the CEO, with sufficient information to enable NZX and ASX change of interests notification; all Directors are to be notified
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately after the trade is completed
clearance.evidence: Once a Restricted Person has completed a trade in the Company Securities, the relevant person described in rule 7, must be immediately: advised that the trade has been completed; and in the case of Directors and Senior Executives, provided with sufficient information to enable the Company to comply with the requirements to notify a change of interests to NZX and ASX

clearance.tier: Other persons identified by the Company from time to time
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately after the trade is completed
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance of any proposed dealing in Company Securities. The notification, which must be made to the person in rule 7, requires the Restricted Person to confirm that they do not hold any inside information.

carve_outs: acquisition of securities under a Company dividend reinvestment plan or employee share plan
participation in any Company employee share or option plan and the exercise of options or rights under those plans
dealings waived under rule 6.5 for exceptional circumstances
short_term.evidence: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.

exceptions.approver: The person specified in rule 7 (the Board for the Chair; the Chair for other Directors and the CEO; the Chair and CEO for Senior Executives; the CEO for other designated persons)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances include severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order or any other circumstances that is deemed exceptional by the person described in rule 7.

If a Restricted Person needs to deal in the Company Securities due to exceptional circumstances but such dealing would breach rule 6.3 or 6.4 of this Policy, the Restricted Person must apply to the person specified in rule 7 for a waiver from compliance with the provisions in rule 6.3 or 6.4.

The additional restrictions in this policy do not prohibit Restricted Persons from acquiring securities under a Company dividend reinvestment plan or an employee share plan, if either plan exists (however, the additional restrictions will apply to any subsequent trading of the Company Securities acquired under those plans).
The additional restrictions in this policy do not affect a Restricted Person's participation in any Company employee share or option plans or the exercise of options/rights under those plans.

financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons; at inception, before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangement or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities; to the rule 7 person (the Board for the Chair, the Chair for other Directors and the CEO, the Chair and CEO for Senior Executives, the CEO for other designated persons); in advance, and the arrangement must not be entered into or the grant made until written clearance is given.

Restricted Persons; on completion of any trade in Company Securities; to the rule 7 person, and for Directors and Senior Executives with sufficient information for NZX and ASX change of interests notices; immediately.

external_documents: Takeovers Code (New Zealand), for the definition of 'associates'
Company employee share and option plans and dividend reinvestment plan rules, referred to but not reproduced
exemption_authority: Rule 6.5: the person specified in rule 7 may grant a written waiver from rule 6.3 (blackout periods) or rule 6.4 (short term trading, speculative gain, short selling) for exceptional circumstances including severe financial hardship, compulsion by a court order, or any other circumstances deemed exceptional. The applicant must apply in writing, explain the circumstances, confirm no inside information, and supply sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action available. A granted waiver lasts 2 business days.
jurisdiction_overlays: New Zealand insider trading law under a dual NZX/ASX listing; associates take their meaning from the New Zealand Takeovers Code
NZX and ASX change of interests notification and the Company's interests register for Directors and Senior Executives

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Restricted Person must not, without prior written approval by the relevant person specified in rule 7, engage in hedging arrangements, deal in derivatives or enter into other arrangements which vary economic risk related to the Company's Securities including, for example ... put and call options ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs of a collar are expressly contemplated and are permissible with prior written approval, so the derivative side of the structure has a clear approval route rather than a prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This provision includes engaging in hedging or other arrangements that have the effect of limiting the economic risk in connection with unvested securities issued pursuant to any employee option or share plan.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unusually, unvested plan securities are brought within the same approval gate rather than an absolute ban, so a collar is not automatically confined to vested shares, although approval over unvested holdings would be difficult to obtain in practice.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must notify the Company in advance before engaging in any margin or securities lending arrangements or granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities. ... The proposed arrangement must not be entered into or grant made until written clearance has been given by the person nominated in rule 7.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is permitted subject to notification and written clearance, so both legs of a funded collar can be approved by the same approver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance to deal in Company Securities can be revoked at any time but will otherwise be valid (unless another period is otherwise specified in the clearance) for a period of ten trading days commencing on the date following the clearance being obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A ten trading day window is long enough to document and price a collar, but the unrestricted revocation right means the bank should not rely on clearance surviving to settlement and should build a termination right for revoked clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In determining whether to clear the proposed dealing, the relevant person nominated in rule 7 will consider whether the proposed dealing is appropriate having regard to all relevant circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no SLA, no criteria and no appeal, so approval of a collar turns entirely on the Chair's or Board's view of appropriateness and cannot be assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Rule 6.10 requires clearance for margin and securities lending and encumbrances but says nothing about margin calls, forced sales, price triggers or what happens if the lender sells during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy gives the executive no protection if the bank enforces during a blackout, so enforcement and physical settlement mechanics must be negotiated into the loan and collar documents rather than relied on from the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other period that the Company specifies from time to time
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ad hoc blackouts with no stated notice or duration can block entry, roll, unwind or settlement of the collar at any time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Restricted Person needs to deal in the Company Securities due to exceptional circumstances ... the Restricted Person must apply to the person specified in rule 7 for a waiver ... in each circumstance the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 2 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A blackout-period unwind or settlement is theoretically possible on a severe financial hardship or court order waiver, but only for 2 business days and only on evidence that dealing is the most reasonable course available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: their associates (as defined in the Takeovers Code)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a spouse, family trust or controlled entity does not avoid the clearance and notification gates, since associates are themselves Restricted Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons should not trade in the Company Securities on a short term basis or for speculative trading gain or short sell any Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: No fixed period is set, so a short-dated collar or one with knock-out features could be characterised as short term or speculative; a longer tenor and physical settlement reduce that risk.

summary: A funded collar is available to a2 Milk Directors and Senior Executives, but only with express prior written approval of both legs. Rule 6.9 names put and call options, equity swaps and arrangements varying economic risk in the Company's Securities, and permits them with prior written approval from the rule 7 approver (the Board for the Chair, the Chair for other Directors and the CEO, the Chair and CEO for Senior Executives); rule 6.10 separately permits granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities, and margin or securities lending, on advance notification plus written clearance, so the loan leg is not prohibited. Approval discretion is unfettered and clearance is revocable at any time and otherwise lasts ten trading days, so the trade must be entered promptly and the bank should provide for revoked clearance. Entry must sit outside the two blackout periods and any ad hoc period the Company specifies, and the arrangement should not look short term or speculative under rule 6.4. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or price triggers, so enforcement mechanics and any blackout-period settlement risk must be handled contractually, with only the 2 business day exceptional circumstances waiver in rule 6.5 as relief.
